overall_reason: A personal long-form essay on a plain WordPress theme, built around the author's real 2004 LinkedIn Series B slides with first-person Context/Advice commentary on each; the copy is specific, dated and falsifiable, and the design makes no attempt at a landing-page look.

findings.evidence: T-FRESH-READER: the h2s alternate 'Context' / 'Advice' 36 times each, so the outline and any skim read carry no information; which slide or topic a section covers is only in the image.
findings.after: Name each pair by its slide, e.g. 'Slide 3: Find and contact the people you need — Context'.
findings.why: Repeated category labels as heads make a 9,400-word piece hard to navigate; the content is specific but the structure hides it.

strengths: T-RIVAL-NAME passes: 'the deck I used to pitch LinkedIn to Greylock for a Series B investment back in 2004', Friendster/MySpace/Benchmark/Kleiner context, 'We changed some of the text... on slides 9, 12-14, 18, 19, 31, and 36' — none of it is transferable.
The original 2004 slides (clip-art people network, blue Arial headline) are shown as historical artefacts, not restyled; honesty about 'many stylistic errors' is part of the voice.

disputed sweep hit: placeholder_residue on 'this is somewhat an empty placeholder' and 'A placeholder slide that says only Appendix' — the word is used in the essay's own advice about decks, not left-over template text.
not_investigated: Theme-level chrome (WordPress/WPBakery markup) is generic but unobtrusive; not judged as slop because the page's content and purpose are authored.
Analytics scripts blocked in capture (manifest network) do not affect the render.
